purpose: Frontier option (A): a LIGAND-ONLY 'connected' rate published ALONGSIDE the metal-inclusive one, to separate 'the metal fell off' from 'the ligand itself fragmented'. Reporting-only. This run measures ONE pool of 2112 rows; whether it reproduces a published rate for this pool is COMPUTED in published_cross_check, not asserted.
direction: single_fragment_rate is HIGHER IS BETTER for both arms, but the ligand-only arm is a DIAGNOSTIC, not a target: a coordination complex is SUPPOSED to have the metal as part of its connectivity, so a low ligand-only rate is not per se a defect. Read the two arms TOGETHER (see verdict).

definitions.metal_symbols_rule: an atom is 'a metal' iff its element symbol is in the repo's canonical d-block TRANSITION_METALS list (Sc..Hg); the trainer's cohort set {Ru,Rh,Re,Os,Ir,Pt} is a subset. Stripping deletes the metal atom and every bond incident to it; nothing else is touched (counterions stay).
definitions.connected_rule: one RDKit connected component AND at least one heavy atom. An empty ligand is NOT connected.
definitions.both_arms_same_code_path: both arms go through arm_stats(), so the metal-inclusive and ligand-only numbers are internally comparable by construction.

denominators.denominator_note: Every rate below is over the n_analyzed rows. A row whose ligand is empty after stripping is NOT connected in either arm and is NOT removed from the denominator; it is counted in n_empty_ligand_after_strip.

metal_inclusive.definition: the whole emitted molecule, exactly as the pool CSV reports it -- the arm a frontier comparison would target.

ligand_only.definition: the SAME molecule with every metal atom deleted (and its bonds removed): the connectivity the organic skeleton has on its own. Not a real molecule -- a counterfactual.

contingency.note: b = the metal fell off and the ligand stayed intact (a metal-coordination failure). c = the whole molecule is one fragment ONLY because the metal bridges otherwise disconnected ligand pieces -- the ligand is fragmented and the metal is hiding it.

paired.n_frags_delta_note: ligand-only n_frags minus metal-inclusive n_frags, per row. Negative = the metal was a fragment of its own (it fell off); positive = the metal was bonding ligand pieces together (removing it splits them).

csv_cross_check.note: The metal-inclusive arm was recomputed from scratch by this tool and compared against the pool's own n_frags_raw / largest_frag_frac columns. Zero mismatches means the two arms are measured over the same molecules by the same definition.

metal_set_invariance.rule: d-block TRANSITION_METALS (the project's own metal predicate)
metal_set_invariance.narrower_rule: the trainer's _TARGET_METALS cohort {Ru, Rh, Re, Os, Ir, Pt}
metal_set_invariance.note: The rule is not pool-fitted: the answer is identical under the project's broad d-block metal predicate and under the narrow trainer cohort set.

verdict.question: How much of the pool's fragmentation is the METAL falling off, versus the LIGAND itself fragmenting?
verdict.conclusion: The 'the metal fell off' hypothesis is REFUTED as the dominant explanation, and the measurement points the other way: only 7 of 2112 rows are 'metal fell off, ligand intact'. The overwhelming majority of the fragmentation is LIGAND-side. Moreover the metal-inclusive rate (0.2505) is much HIGHER than the ligand-only rate (0.0284) because in 476 rows the whole molecule is one fragment ONLY because the metal bridges otherwise-disconnected ligand pieces. So the metal-inclusive 'connected' count is largely the metal CONCEALING ligand fragmentation, not the ligand being intact -- the repair effort belongs on the ligand skeleton, not on keeping the metal attached. This is an honest negative for the metal-falls-off hypothesis and a positive finding that the metal is a connectivity hub.

premise_checks.brief_claim: the task brief asserted that the rows whose metal is alone in its fragment are exactly the rows whose ligand becomes empty after stripping.
premise_checks.explanation: In every one of the metal-alone rows the row ALSO carries ligand-bearing fragments, so stripping the metal leaves a non-empty ligand. The genuinely empty-ligand case -- a row that is metal and nothing else -- has count 0 on this pool. The two quantities are reported under separate names so the distinction survives.

end_to_end_headline.definition: 'one connected, parseable molecule per DRAWN sample', median over the generation-side runs

published_cross_check.rule: a published artifact is compared ONLY when its own source_pool names THIS pool; the comparison is computed, never asserted
published_cross_check.verdict: THIS RUN REPRODUCES the published rate for THIS pool exactly (bit-for-bit)

not_comparable_to.end_to_end_median_headline: metrics/by_metric/cfm_fragmentation_audit.json -> /summary/generation_side/single_molecule_rate_end_to_end is an END-TO-END rate over 9 RUNS of a different quantity ('one connected parseable molecule per DRAWN sample'). This metric is a per-ROW paired analysis over ONE pool of 2112 rows.
not_comparable_to.other_pools_single_pool_counts: the metal-inclusive arm of THIS tool is a single-pool rate for THIS pool only; it is reported so the two arms are comparable. The NEW quantity is the ligand-only rate, over a NEW denominator definition. Which published number (if any) this run reproduces is COMPUTED in published_cross_check -- it is not asserted here.

comparability.statement: These numbers are NOT comparable to the published frontier band of 92.7-94 %. 4 independent breaks separate them, and all 4 must hold simultaneously for any comparison to be meaningful.

breaks.frontier: 92.7-94 % is measured over 10,000-15,000 generated molecules from a training-set-distribution sampling.
breaks.ours: ONE pool of 2112 rows from ONE post-hoc decode (cfm_c8_fullgen_2026_10_24/generated_smiles.csv).

breaks.frontier: 'connected' there means the DECODER's own connectivity claim; 'valid' means RDKit sanitisation; '% PB-Valid' means PoseBusters geometry.
breaks.ours: an RDKit connected-component count of the emitted SMILES. The ligand-only arm additionally deletes the metal atom(s) first, which is a counterfactual the frontier papers do not publish.

breaks.frontier: under the `band_provenance` reading the band's two endpoints are RAW (post_processed: false in that reading), while the competing `sources`.`EF-TALFM` reading pairs a raw connectivity cell with a post-processed companion cell -- so whether the band as a whole is RAW is NOT settled on disk, and which frontier cells the band names is NOT settled on disk: the repo holds TWO competing provenance readings for it, both recorded in the frontier post-processing matrix record (`frontier_matrix.json`) -- the first under `band_provenance`, the second under `sources`.`EF-TALFM` -- and they do not even agree on the numerals. Under BOTH readings the band is external, is NOT one homogeneous quantity, and is NOT on our scale -- so the post-processing axis is a THIRD, separate axis on top of the METRIC break, not the break itself.
breaks.ours: every number here is RAW -- the SMILES exactly as the sampler emitted it, no LargestFragmentChooser, no explicit H, no UFF.

breaks.frontier: the frontier dataset carries explicit hydrogens.
breaks.ours: our pool does not (implicit H), which changes both sanitisation and geometry.
